bindings.label: A 72-year-old woman experienced behavioural changes, unsteadiness, and frequent falls over the past year

Over the past year, relatives reported that she became listless, neglected work and domestic activities, exhibited hyperreligious behaviour, anxiety, loss of appetite, mild lower limb weakness, and falls; later she had episodes of agitation, confusion, and visual hallucinations, leading to initiation of antipsychotic medication, and eventually lost the ability to walk and became wheelchair-bound

On admission, she showed disorientation, apathy, apraxia, short-term memory deficit (MMSE = 7), anosmia, mild flaccid proximal paraparesis, and muscular atrophy; patellar reflexes and plantar responses were normal; urinary incontinence was present without signs of sensory impairment
She had started oral anticoagulant therapy two years earlier due to paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; 24-hour Holter monitoring revealed no paroxysmal atrial fibrillation

A comprehensive workup including vitamin levels, thyroid function, tumour markers, full-body CT, and breast ultrasound was unremarkable; EEG indicated diffuse cerebral dysfunction without epileptic activity
